title: What tools do you wish existed for AI-assisted game dev?
author: GeneralAdvantage2950
selftext:
I'm a solo dev, and I'm building some tools in this space. Before I go further, I want to make sure I'm solving real problems and not just my own.

Most of us are using Claude Code, Cursor, or ChatGPT for code, plus a mix of other tools for art, audio, and writing. But a lot of the workflow still feels like duct tape.

A few questions:

1. What part of your workflow is the most painful right now?

2. Is there a tool you wish existed? A few ideas I've been thinking about:

   \- a) Something that keeps AI-generated art in a consistent style

   \- b) Something that helps build characters and worlds with real depth

   \- c) Something that keeps your design docs in sync with your code

   Would any of those actually help, or are they already solved for you?

3. What tools have you tried and dropped, and why?

comments.author: jildos_legoplanet
comments.body: The ability to have ChatGPT and Codex speak to eachother

replies.author: GeneralAdvantage2950
replies.body: Do you mean in real time?

replies.author: jildos_legoplanet
replies.body: Yeah pretty much.. i’m constantly couriering github issued/pull requests between one and the other. I know i can have Codex do all of that but ChatGPT is way more critical doing code reviews and it costs me a fraction of tokens this way

replies.author: M4xs0n
replies.body: I am doing the Same but you are a Genius. Do you use Git for your project and Connect ChatGPT with Github so it Can Check the Updates on its own?

comments.author: Vumsy101
comments.body:
Rigging, posing and animating rigs in a way that is editable by a human later. Training an AI to play your game in a more accessible way.

Aside from that, usual memory shit. Remembering to keep code consistent and keep more holistic track of it.

Honestly though, the goal of AI should be to make genres less gate kept by team size. So whatever traditionally require a lot of hands on deck is where it's at. It does it well for boilerplate coding, so that's amazing, but it's still pretty lacking in the asset volume department. Printing models and character animations quickly.

If a solo dev can create double A sized games in 5 years, AI has reached what I consider its goal.

replies.author: Will_X_Intent
replies.body: I think we are there.  In 1 year, they can do it in 2.  Two years from now, they can do it in a month.  5 years and it's happening real time

comments.author: Will_X_Intent
comments.body: I think a lot of people would benefit from will organized design and development documents that route AI to the exact information it needs and nothing more.

replies.author: GeneralAdvantage2950
replies.body:
So a place where the design doc lives and a structure allows ai to grab the correct data?

My thoughts go to an app that attaches to the engine and can help create game play systems.

Do you have an example of what you are thinking?

replies.author: M4xs0n
replies.body: No, not an app that you can sell. An open Database that guides the LLM if it comes across problems that someone else already solved

replies.author: Will_X_Intent
replies.body: People keep trying to have AI make things to sell, but AI makes that proposition... Dumb.  We need to go back to the early days of the Internet where people made cool stuff and gave it away

replies.author: aigamedev-ModTeam
replies.body: Be respectul to others and follow reddits guidelines and policies.

comments.author: rookan
comments.body: I hate to constantly keep an eye on Context Window in Claude Code desktop app. It has 1M context window but I try to start new session when hitting 300K or more context. I created a /handover skill but it is still tedious process - end current session, start new one just to continue working on new features.  I just want to keep working on new features, fixing bugs in the same window. Maybe I just use AI tools wrong. What's your opinion?

replies.author: rookan
replies.body: compress is stupid and does not save important info

comments.author: HugoDzz
comments.body:
The truth is that LLMs are very, very smart nowadays. And we can build pretty much any tool we want, and this is accelerating.

I think the best way to discover great tools opportunities (I build my own), is to experience the pain point yourself making games.
